paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. God's people were quoting a proverb: 'The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the teeth of the children are set on edge' (Ezekiel 18:2). It was a nice way to say 'None of this is on us,' but God says 'The soul who sins is the one who will die,' and He says it twice (Ezekiel 18:4, 20).

This is good news AND a wake-up call, so hold on. Your father's sins don't get stamped on your cookie box, and your father's goodness doesn't get stamped there either. Each person stands before God for their own life (Ezekiel 18:20). So when Israel says, 'The way of the Lord is not just,' God turns it right back: 'Is it not your ways that are unjust?' (Ezekiel 18:29). I know that stings, because blaming somebody else is the easiest recipe in the world.

Now look at the door God leaves wide open. A wicked man who turns will live, and none of his transgressions will be held against him (Ezekiel 18:21-22). God asks, 'Do I take any pleasure in the death of the wicked?' (Ezekiel 18:23). So He says, 'Cast away from yourselves all the transgressions you have committed, and fashion for yourselves a new heart and a new spirit' (Ezekiel 18:31). That's the invitation for you today, baker: 'So repent and live!' (Ezekiel 18:32). And hear this part loud and clear: it's never too late to turn.
